content.text: [Slack #data-team chen_hao Mon Mar 10 09:00 CST 2026] Hey team, I've been looking at the 618 GMV data and there's a calibration issue. The v1 data file (gmv_daily_618_v1.csv) uses Method 1 GMV calibration for the period 2025-05-13 to 2025-05-22. That means those 10 days have GMV overstated by roughly 6-7%. We need to switch to Method 2 for the official report.

Confirmed: the v1 GMV data for 2025-05-13 through 2025-05-22 uses Method 1 calibration (excludes only >RMB 2,000 unfulfilled orders). Official reporting requires Method 2 (also excludes >RMB 100k + daily spend >RMB 1M + platform subsidies). I'll flag this in the data quality report and use v2 when available.
[Slack #data-team li_wei Mon Mar 10 09:15 CST 2026] Also, there's been a debate about whether platform subsidies count toward GMV. Can someone clarify?

Per context/metric_definitions.md section 1: GMV is computed BEFORE deducting subsidies per the standard definition (Wall Street Prep), BUT LinkMart's internal Method 2 calibration explicitly excludes platform subsidies from GMV to align with the official JD reporting standard. So the answer depends on which calibration you're using: the standard GMV formula does not exclude subsidies, but Method 2 does.

[Slack #data-team chen_hao Mon Mar 10 09:30 CST 2026] And one more thing: I see the preliminary report draft uses ×365 for inventory days calculation. That's wrong. Our JD-aligned formula uses ×360 specifically (see metric_definitions.md section 3). The ×365 formula is from the generic Onramp Funds benchmark.

Confirmed: LinkMart uses the JD official formula with multiplier ×360 (not ×365). The ×365 figure appears only in the legacy report and generic industry references — not applicable to our official KPI computation. I'll ensure all inventory day calculations use (avg_inventory_5q / ttm_cogs) × 360.
